transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-21
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 53 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Ellis (Redwood AE), Samira Patel (Redwood SE), Avery Cho (Redwood AM), Carlos Mendes (CTO, Neptune), Priya Nair (Head of Security, Neptune), Liam O'Connor (DevOps, Neptune), Maya Ruiz (Product, Neptune)

Summary:
Initial security posture intake for Neptune Works evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment. Focus areas: SOC2/ISO certification needs, SSO/SAML and enterprise IdP, RBAC and least-privilege, audit logs retention and exportability, encryption keys/KMS/HSM options, data residency and retention windows. Customer wants decision criteria and checklist to present to procurement and security council next week.

Topics covered:
- Compliance baseline: SOC2/ISO-27001 coverage (which controls are in scope)
- Identity: SSO, SAML, SCIM, provisioning, RBAC models
- Cryptography: at-rest and in-transit, customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) options
- Observability/Audit: retention, export, access logs, SIEM integration
- Deployment modes: tradeoffs (latency vs isolation vs cost) between Hosted/Dedicated/Private
- Data retention and deletion guarantees / e-discovery support

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Jordan from Redwood, appreciate you carving out the time, uh quick roll call?
[00:07] Carlos: hi Carlos here, CTO, thanks.
[00:10] Priya: Priya, Head of Security.
[00:12] Liam: Liam, DevOps.
[00:14] Maya: Maya from Prod.
[00:15] Samira: Samira SE and I'll be leading the deeper tech follow-up.
[00:20] Jordan: awesome. Broadly what we want to do is understand your security constraints and what will make your security council comfortable — especially around keys, auditability, and where data lives. Quick high level from you Carlos, what's driving the evaluation?
[00:35] Carlos: yeah, so we are building an assistant for our enterprise customers that surfaces internal docs, code snippets, api keys redacted etc so we have to be able to prove to customers and auditors that their PII and secrets won't leak and we can meet contractual retention and deletion windows. We're also looking at long term cost for high throughput requests.
[00:54] Priya: to add, procurement has asked for SOC2 evidence or equivalent, and if we go private they want to know what controls we still need to own. Also looking at SAML/SSO integration and fine grained RBAC — we can't have engineers see certain datasets.
[01:12] Samira: ok makes sense. At a high level Redwood has three serving modes — hosted API, dedicated capacity, and private (VPC / on-prem). Quick callout: our SOC2 covers the hosted platform controls currently, we also have ISO-27001 in flight (small note: the transcript may say I-S-O 27 0 1 or iso twenty sevn), and for Dedicated/Private we provide the same control plane plus additional isolation depending on the option.
[01:42] Priya: can you clarify "same control plane"— if we do Private on our VPC who's responsible for patching, who's responsible for key custody?
[01:53] Samira: good question. For Private we offer a customer-managed control plane option — meaning you get the control plane deployed into your VPC, Redwood provides the images and ops runbook. Patch responsibilities are shared: you run host-level patching if you're on the fully private/on-prem model, if it's private but hosted in our managed private tenancy we handle underlying patching. For keys you can bring-your-own-KMS — we integrate via standard KMS APIs or via HSM with a vault.
[02:20] Liam: when you say bring-your-own-KMS, do you support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault? And do you do envelope encryption?
[02:27] Samira: yes we support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and Azure Key Vault, and for on-prem we support HSM endpoints and bring-your-own-key via a customer-managed vault. We use enveloping — root key in your KMS, data keys used ephemeral in service. Note sometimes the notes transcribe K-V cache as "kv cash" — we do use KV cache for context, that is not persisted to customer bucket unless configured.
[02:50] Priya: ok retention — we need logs for 1 year and audit trail for admin actions for 7 years in some contracts, are those configurable?
[02:59] Jordan: yes audit logs retention is configurable in Dedicated and Private. For Hosted we provide 90-day retention by default but we can offer extended retention as an add-on and can stream logs to your SIEM via Kafka or S3 export.
[03:12] Maya: what's in the audit logs? full prompts? masked?
[03:16] Samira: good call — we redact secrets out-of-the-box from the UI exports, but raw request/response artifacts are stored encrypted. For customers with stricter needs we can route raw telemetry to your S3 or your tenant bucket and you control lifecycle and purging.
[03:33] Carlos: encryption at rest — are model weights encrypted? where are embeddings stored?
[03:38] Samira: model weights are managed by Redwood, hosted in encrypted storage. Customer data — embeddings and prompt history — are stored in your tenant space for Dedicated/Private. For Hosted, by default data is logically multitenant and encrypted, but we have options to isolate data per tenant and to enable customer-managed keys.
[03:58] Priya: SOC2 evidence — can you share the scope and last audit date? Also any open findings in the last audit?
[04:05] Jordan: we'll send the SOC2 Type II summary. Last audit date was 2026-03, no critical findings, a few low-level ops items that were closed. I'll attach the audit letter and the bridge letter.
[04:20] Priya: do you have pen test results?
[04:23] Jordan: yes we do quarterly pentests by a third party, recent report available, we'll redact sensitive vuln details but share the exec summary.
[04:32] Liam: network connectivity for private — does Redwood support private peering and dedicated network links?
[04:36] Samira: yes we support cross-account VPC peering, PrivateLink style endpoints, and VPN/Direct Connect integrations for high-throughput private connectivity on Dedicated/Private.
[04:47] Carlos: latency — if we move to Dedicated vs Hosted what's the typical delta? ops for 3ms p50 to 20ms or?
[04:54] Samira: depends on model and sequence length — Dedicated generally reduces variance and can improve p50/p95 — we've seen 10-30% improvement in P50 for similar hardware because of pinned pools and reduced tenant noise. For strict p99 SLAs Private on co-located infra is where you get the most stable tail latencies.
[05:14] Maya: procurement asked about contractual SLAs and breach notifications — what's your standard term?
[05:18] Jordan: our Hosted SLA is 99.9% uptime for inference APIs, Dedicated can get higher contractual guarantees and Private bespoke SLAs; breach notifications include 72-hour initial notification and postmortem within 14 days. We'll share the SLA appendix.
[05:33] [Speaker 3, possible mislabel]: um yeah need to check legal for indemnities.
[05:38] Priya: RBAC — can we create roles that restrict specific dataset access or only route/rate limit at API key level?
[05:44] Samira: we have token-level RBAC with scopes, and for Dedicated/Private we support namespaced roles that map down to dataset-level access controls. There's a UI and an API, and you can sync groups from your IdP via SCIM.
[05:58] Liam: SAML + SCIM — any quirks? We have Okta and OneLogin.
[06:03] Samira: Okta and OneLogin are supported. For SAML we support IdP-initiated and SP-initiated flows, and group sync via SCIM is supported for provisioning. Note: some customers want just SAML without SCIM, which is fine but provisioning becomes manual.
[06:17] Carlos: data residency — we need EU hosting for EU customers, can you guarantee region pinning?
[06:22] Jordan: yes we offer region pinning; Hosted has regions in US/EU/APAC, Dedicated also can be provisioned in specific cloud regions, and Private is fully under your control so you can keep everything in your EU tenancy.
[06:35] Priya: deletion and e-discovery — how do you handle legal hold?
[06:40] Samira: we can implement retention policies and legal hold flags at tenant-level for Dedicated/Private. For Hosted we can place retention holds on your exported buckets; raw request stores are encrypted and can be purged on request subject to legal constraints. We will produce a deletion certificate for compliance.
[07:00] Maya: are there any operational controls we need to accept in our contract if we go Private? like telemetry or health pings back to Redwood?
[07:08] Samira: in fully private/on-prem deployments, telemetry is opt-in; in managed private we do health pings for orchestration. We can provide a telemetry-redaction configuration and a privacy-level toggle in the ops runbook.
[07:24] Carlos: curious about service account access — how are support engineers given time-limited access for troubleshooting?
[07:29] Jordan: we use just-in-time (JIT) access and ephemeral sessions via our access broker. For Dedicated/Private we can require tickets and provide time-limited credentials scoped to a session, with audit logs recorded.
[07:41] Priya: SIEM integration — can logs be streamed to Splunk or Datadog?
[07:45] Samira: yes Splunk, Datadog, Sumo, and generic syslog/Kafka/S3 sinks are supported. We also support pushing to a customer's private Kafka.
[07:55] Liam: about cost — if we enable long retention and stream raw logs to our S3, what's pricing model?
[07:59] Jordan: retention and log export are generally add-ons, priced based on volume and throughput. We'll provide a pricing estimate based on Neptune's anticipated QPS and retention windows.
[08:12] Carlos: ok can you walk through a hypothetical private deployment flow?
[08:16] Samira: sure — quick overview: requirements intake -> infra sizing (we size GPUs, memory, network) -> infra prep (VPC, subnets, route tables, KMS endpoints) -> deploy control plane images -> runbook handoff and validation -> pilot -> roll to prod. Each step maps to artifacts we provide: terraform modules, helm charts, and an ops runbook.
[08:40] Priya: for KMS we prefer a BYOK model where keys never leave our control — will Redwood support envelope encryption with us holding the root key?
[08:48] Samira: absolutely. Our envelope flow keeps the root key in your KMS; we rotate data keys and do not persist root material. We can also integrate with HSM modules where keys are non-exportable.
[08:58] Maya: is there an option to run model execution on air-gapped infra? some of our customers need that for certain contracts.
[09:04] Samira: yes air-gapped is supported but it's a heavyweight scenario — we provide an on-prem bundle and ops checklist, and you handle offline model loading and updates via signed artifacts.
[09:16] [00:09:40] Carlos: one more on logging — would Redwood ever access customer raw prompts for debugging without explicit permission?
[09:24] Jordan: no. Support access is ticketed and requires JIT approval. For Hosted we may request a redacted sample; but without explicit approval we do not access raw customer data.
[09:36] Priya: ok show me a mapping between your SOC2 controls and our internal control set — do you have a weave or a matrix?
[09:42] Jordan: yes we have a control mapping matrix. We'll send the SOC2 mapping doc that ties controls to AICPA trust services criteria and to common ISO/PCI controls.
[09:50] Maya: timeline — procurement wants recommendation by next Tuesday, is that realistic?
[09:55] Jordan: yes if we share the SOC2 and a Private/Dedicated checklist today, and schedule a 1-hour SE deep dive by Friday, we can give a recommendation and cost estimate by Monday.
[10:06] Priya: one wrinkle — our legal would like to see encryption key escrow options and escrow terms, any precedent?
[10:13] Jordan: we do not escrow customer keys centrally; we can provide attestation letters and contractual commitments about key usage. For very special cases we can discuss an escrow arrangement but that's rare.
[10:24] Liam: about telemetry retention for debugging — what's default for traces and metrics?
[10:29] Samira: traces/metrics default 30 days, can be extended and exported. Logs are separate.
[10:34] Carlos: have you had customers ask for vertical separation — e.g., compute in one region storage in another?
[10:40] Samira: yes some regulated customers do that; we work with them to map data flows. It becomes more complex for KV cache and latency-sensitive use cases but it's doable.
[10:52] Maya: are there any common gotchas companies hit when switching from Hosted to Dedicated?
[10:57] Samira: yes usually under-provisioning network IOPS or not accounting for bursty inference patterns causes throttling; also key management expectations — onboarding KMS often takes longer than teams plan. We'll give a sizing template.
[11:12] Priya: can you provide sample contract language for data ownership and controller/processor roles? we need that for legal review.
[11:18] Jordan: yes we'll include the DPA and sample clauses.
[11:22] Carlos: any open security advisories we should be aware of?
[11:26] Samira: none at the moment; we track advisories and will share the security bulletins feed.
[11:31] Jordan: great, I think we covered the main things. quick recap of next steps — I'll send SOC2 artifacts, pen test executive summary, SLA appendix, and the control mapping matrix. Samira will set up the SE deep dive and prep the Private/Dedicated ops checklist. Liam will share KMS vendor and retention details. Anything else?
[11:52] Priya: if you can also include sample RBAC rules and SCIM mapping that'd be helpful.
[11:57] Jordan: copy that — we'll include that.
[12:00] Carlos: thanks all.

Closing notes / Action summary (auto):
- Jordan: send SOC2 Type II summary, pen test exec summary, SLA appendix, control mapping matrix, RBAC examples.
- Samira: prepare Private/Dedicated ops checklist, sizing template, KMS integration diagram.
- Liam (Neptune): share KMS vendor and retention policy; coordinate SE deep dive availability.

End of transcript.
